items: Name amnesty: everyone's saved name has been reset, so set your real one when the app asks (it also lives in settings). Pick another joke name and you will be found.

Requests can now carry a comment: tap "Add a comment" next to the quick-add field, or fill in the optional box when confirming a request from the room, and the note shows under the tune ("it's Sam's birthday!").
The full-app link now always opens the full app, even on a phone that's been living in the requests view. The request link keeps that phone in the room view as before.

Every session now has its own songbook: pick it when planning the night (the usual book is preselected), and everyone who joins searches that book. Need to switch mid-session? The songbook setting now changes it for the whole session at once.

Thumbs up now works on Up next as well as the pool, so the room can still say it wants a tune after it's been queued. The running order doesn't budge: the count is a nudge for whoever's picking, not a re-sort.

The request link now opens and closes itself around the night, half an hour before start until 4am by default. The share panel switch still overrides it: force it open, close it early, or set your own times instead.

The request link now shows the whole night: Up next and the played count appear above the pool, so a phone on the room view can follow the set as it happens. Looking only, of course. The running order still belongs to the stage.

One planned night at a time: while a session is coming up, starting another shared one is blocked — open the planned night instead, so requests don't split across two half-started Tuesdays. Unlisted sessions are unaffected.
The home screen now leads with Coming up: the next session shows as a big card, so on a club night one tap gets you in, and a night set up in advance is right there for early requests.
Further prepped nights queue under the same heading, and past nights have moved to their own list below, with older ones tucked behind a tap.

Requesting from the room now asks you to confirm before your tune goes in, because there's no taking it back once it's in the pool. There's also a minute's pause between requests, so one very keen phone can't fill the whole night on its own.

Had enough requests? Switch the request link to View only in the share panel. People can still open it and watch tonight's pool, they just can't add to it, and the whiteboard of wishes carries on as usual.

Say what you want to play: give any request a thumbs up and the pool sorts itself, most wanted first. Everyone gets one vote per song, phones on the request link included, and asking for a song already counts as yours. Songs off the whiteboard start level with the rest, so nothing is penalised for arriving on the board.

Take requests from the room: “Share request link” in the share panel opens a requests-only view. Anyone who gets the link can add tunes (with their name) from their own phone, without being able to touch the running order.

Every night is now its own session, named by its date. Starting a new one no longer wipes the last, and the app opens on the club's session history so you can revisit a past night or set one up in advance.

Now called Setlister, the app got a session-screen redesign: the night's date is the title, the next tune is highlighted, adding by name sits right above the request pool, a fresh night opens on just the camera, and copy/download live on the “Up next” heading.

Snapping the board is faster and no longer a one-way wait: the photo is shrunk on your phone before it's sent, clear matches go straight to Requests (you only review what the scanner wasn't sure about, and nothing already listed is added twice), and a slow scan can be cancelled instead of leaving you stuck.
See who's here: shared sessions show everyone currently connected.
Played songs collapse into a one-line count above Up next.
The Bin now lives inside Requests as a collapsed group.
Swipe a song sideways to move it between Up next and Requests.
Drag-to-reorder now follows your finger.
Share a session: everyone with the link sees the same lists, live.
Set your name in settings, and songs will show who added them.
Swipe right to mark a song played, swipe left to bin it.
Requests and Up next are separate lists. Promote what you'll actually play.
Type-ahead songbook search when adding a request by name.
First version: snap the request whiteboard and get a songbook-matched setlist.
